```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=FALSE}
# ============================================================================
# DATA PREPARATION
# ============================================================================

load("SatData.RData")

# Clean column names and prepare numeric data
prepare_data <- function(data) {
  # Fix column names
  names(data) <- make.names(names(data), unique = TRUE)
  
  # Extract numeric variables and handle missing values
  num_vars <- data %>% 
    select_if(is.numeric) %>%
    mutate_all(~ifelse(is.na(.), mean(., na.rm = TRUE), .))
  
  return(list(full_data = data, numeric_data = num_vars))
}

data_clean <- prepare_data(satisfaction)
num_vars <- data_clean$numeric_data
satisfaction <- data_clean$full_data

# Data overview
str(satisfaction)
summary(satisfaction)

# ============================================================================
# UTILITY FUNCTIONS
# ============================================================================

# Function to extract top loadings from PCA/FA
get_top_loadings <- function(loadings_matrix, component, n = 5) {
  loadings_sorted <- sort(abs(loadings_matrix[, component]), decreasing = TRUE)
  top_vars <- names(loadings_sorted)[1:n]
  data.frame(
    Variable = top_vars, 
    Loading = loadings_matrix[top_vars, component]
  )
}

# Function to determine optimal number of components
find_optimal_components <- function(pca_result, variance_threshold = 0.90) {
  var_prop <- (pca_result$sdev^2) / sum(pca_result$sdev^2)
  cumvar <- cumsum(var_prop)
  optimal_n <- which(cumvar >= variance_threshold)[1]
  
  return(list(
    var_explained = var_prop,
    cumulative_var = cumvar,
    optimal_components = optimal_n
  ))
}

# ============================================================================
# PRINCIPAL COMPONENT ANALYSIS
# ============================================================================

perform_pca <- function(data) {
  pca_result <- prcomp(data, center = TRUE, scale. = FALSE)
  variance_info <- find_optimal_components(pca_result)
  
  message("Components needed for 90% variance: ", variance_info$optimal_components)
  
  # Display first 6 components variance
  variance_table <- rbind(
    var_prop = variance_info$var_explained[1:6],
    cumvar = variance_info$cumulative_var[1:6]
  )
  print(round(variance_table, 4))
  
  # Show top loadings for first 6 components
  for (i in 1:6) {
    message("PC", i, " top loadings:")
    print(get_top_loadings(pca_result$rotation, i, 6))
  }
  
  return(list(
    pca = pca_result,
    variance_info = variance_info
  ))
}

pca_results <- perform_pca(num_vars)

# ============================================================================
# FACTOR ANALYSIS
# ============================================================================

perform_factor_analysis <- function(data, n_factors = 6) {
  fa_result <- factanal(data, factors = n_factors, rotation = "varimax")
  
  print(fa_result)
  print(fa_result$loadings, cutoff = 0.3)
  
  return(fa_result)
}

fa_results <- perform_factor_analysis(num_vars)

# ============================================================================
# VISUALIZATIONS
# ============================================================================

create_pca_plots <- function(pca_result) {
  par(mfrow = c(2, 1))
  
  # Scree plot
  fviz_eig(pca_result, addlabels = TRUE, ncp = min(10, ncol(num_vars)))
  
  # Biplot
  fviz_pca_biplot(pca_result, repel = TRUE)
}

create_pca_plots(pca_results$pca)

# ============================================================================
# FACTOR SCORES AND CLUSTERING
# ============================================================================

calculate_factor_scores <- function(data) {
  # Calculate Bartlett factor scores
  fa_with_scores <- factanal(
    ~ reputation + trustworthiness + seriousness + solidness + care + 
      exp_products + exp_services + service + solutions + quality + 
      qual_products + qual_services + range_products + qual_personal + 
      qual_overall + benefits + investments + quality.1 + price + 
      satisfaction + expectations + comparison + performance + return + 
      switch + recommendation + loyalty,
    factors = 6, 
    data = data, 
    scores = "Bartlett"
  )
  
  return(fa_with_scores$scores)
}

factor_scores <- calculate_factor_scores(num_vars)

# Display factor scores (first 6 observations)
print(head(factor_scores))

# Plot first two factors
plot(factor_scores[,1], factor_scores[,2], pch = 19,
     main = "Factor Scores (Factors 1 & 2)",
     xlab = "Factor 1", ylab = "Factor 2")

# ============================================================================
# CLUSTERING ANALYSIS
# ============================================================================

perform_clustering <- function(pca_result, k = 4, n_components = 4) {
  # Use first n components for clustering
  pc_scores <- pca_result$x[, 1:n_components]
  
  # K-means clustering
  set.seed(123)  # For reproducibility
  kmeans_result <- kmeans(pc_scores, centers = k, nstart = 25)
  
  print(table(kmeans_result$cluster))
  
  # Silhouette analysis
  sil_analysis <- silhouette(kmeans_result$cluster, dist(pc_scores))
  avg_silhouette <- mean(sil_analysis[, 3])
  message("Average silhouette width: ", round(avg_silhouette, 3))
  
  # Hierarchical clustering
  distance_matrix <- dist(pc_scores)
  hclust_result <- hclust(distance_matrix, method = "ward.D2")
  
  # Plot dendrogram
  plot(hclust_result, main = "Hierarchical Clustering (Ward.D2)")
  rect.hclust(hclust_result, k = k)
  
  return(list(
    pc_scores = pc_scores,
    kmeans = kmeans_result,
    hclust = hclust_result,
    silhouette_avg = avg_silhouette
  ))
}

clustering_results <- perform_clustering(pca_results$pca)

# ============================================================================
# SEGMENT PROFILING
# ============================================================================

create_segment_profiles <- function(original_data, clustering_result) {
  # Add cluster assignments to original data
  segmented_data <- original_data %>%
    mutate(segment_kmeans = factor(clustering_result$kmeans$cluster))
  
  # Create segment summary
  segment_summary <- segmented_data %>%
    group_by(segment_kmeans) %>%
    summarise_all(~if(is.numeric(.)) mean(., na.rm = TRUE) else first(.))
  
  return(list(
    segmented_data = segmented_data,
    summary = segment_summary
  ))
}

segment_profiles <- create_segment_profiles(satisfaction, clustering_results)

# ============================================================================
# LINEAR DISCRIMINANT ANALYSIS
# ============================================================================

perform_lda <- function(pc_scores, cluster_assignments) {
  # Prepare data for LDA
  lda_data <- data.frame(
    pc_scores,
    segment = factor(cluster_assignments)
  )
  
  # Fit LDA model
  lda_model <- lda(segment ~ ., data = lda_data)
  
  print(lda_model)
  
  # Create LDA plot
  plot(lda_model, main = "Linear Discriminant Analysis")
  
  # Calculate prediction accuracy
  predictions <- predict(lda_model)$class
  accuracy <- mean(predictions == lda_data$segment)
  message("Classification accuracy: ", round(accuracy, 3))
  
  return(list(
    model = lda_model,
    predictions = predictions,
    accuracy = accuracy
  ))
}

lda_results <- perform_lda(clustering_results$pc_scores, clustering_results$kmeans$cluster)

# ============================================================================
# KEY INSIGHTS & VISUALIZATIONS FOR PRESENTATION
# ============================================================================

# Create comprehensive visualization dashboard
create_presentation_plots <- function() {
  # Set up multi-panel layout
  par(mfrow = c(2, 3), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 2))
  
  # 1. Satisfaction distribution by gender
  boxplot(satisfaction ~ gender, data = satisfaction,
          main = "Spokojenost dle pohlaví zákazníka",
          ylab = "Skóre spokojenosti", col = c("lightblue", "lightcoral"))
  
  # 2. Top 5 variables correlation with satisfaction
  cor_with_sat <- cor(num_vars$satisfaction, num_vars)[1,]
  top_cors <- sort(abs(cor_with_sat), decreasing = TRUE)[2:6]  # Exclude self-correlation
  barplot(top_cors, main = "Top 5 prediktorů spokojenosti zákazníků",
          ylab = "Korelace", las = 2, col = "steelblue")
  
  # 3. Cluster comparison - key metrics
  cluster_means <- aggregate(cbind(satisfaction, loyalty, recommendation) ~ 
                           factor(clustering_results$kmeans$cluster), 
                           data = satisfaction, mean)
  barplot(t(as.matrix(cluster_means[,-1])), beside = TRUE,
          main = "Klíčové metriky v jednotlivých segmentech",
          legend = c("Spokojenost", "Věrnost", "Doporučili by dále"),
          col = c("gold", "lightgreen", "salmon"))
  
  # 4. PCA Variance Explained
  barplot(pca_results$variance_info$var_explained[1:8],
          main = "PCA Vysvětlená variabilita",
          xlab = "Hlavní komponenta", ylab = "Podíl variability",
          col = "lightblue", names.arg = paste0("PC", 1:8))
  
  # 5. Factor loadings heatmap (simplified)
  top_factors <- fa_results$loadings[,1:3]
  image(1:3, 1:nrow(top_factors), t(as.matrix(top_factors)),
        main = "Faktorové zatížení (Top 3)",
        xlab = "Faktor", ylab = "", col = heat.colors(20),
        axes = FALSE)
  axis(1, at = 1:3, labels = paste0("F", 1:3))
  axis(2, at = 1:nrow(top_factors), labels = rownames(top_factors), las = 2, cex.axis = 0.7)
  
  # 6. Segment sizes pie chart
  pie(table(clustering_results$kmeans$cluster),
      main = "Zákaznické segmenty",
      labels = paste0("Seg ", 1:4, "\n(", table(clustering_results$kmeans$cluster), ")"),
      col = rainbow(4))
  
  par(mfrow = c(1, 1))  # Reset layout
}

create_presentation_plots()

# Generate key statistics table
generate_key_insights <- function() {
  # Sample characteristics
  gender_dist <- table(satisfaction$gender)
  message("Sample: 250 customers (", gender_dist["female"], "F, ", gender_dist["male"], "M)")
  
  # Satisfaction metrics
  sat_stats <- summary(satisfaction$satisfaction)
  message("Satisfaction: Mean = ", round(sat_stats["Mean"], 1), 
      ", Range = ", sat_stats["Min."], "-", sat_stats["Max."])
  
  # Top satisfaction drivers
  cor_matrix <- cor(num_vars)
  sat_correlations <- cor_matrix[,"satisfaction"]
  top_drivers <- names(sort(abs(sat_correlations), decreasing = TRUE)[2:4])
  message("Top drivers: ", paste(top_drivers, collapse = ", "))
  
  # Factor analysis summary
  message("Factors explain ", round(sum(fa_results$loadings^2)/length(num_vars) * 100, 1), 
      "% of total variance")
  
  # Segment characteristics
  seg_data <- satisfaction %>%
    mutate(segment = clustering_results$kmeans$cluster) %>%
    group_by(segment) %>%
    summarise(
      size = n(),
      avg_satisfaction = round(mean(satisfaction), 1),
      avg_loyalty = round(mean(loyalty), 1),
      pct_high_satisfaction = round(mean(satisfaction >= 8) * 100, 0)
    )
  
  print(seg_data)
  
  return(seg_data)
}

insights_table <- generate_key_insights()

# Create executive summary table
create_summary_table <- function() {
  summary_data <- data.frame(
    Metric = c("Sample Size", "Avg Satisfaction", "Avg Loyalty", "Top Driver", 
               "Segments Identified", "Best Segment Size", "Classification Accuracy"),
    Value = c("250", round(mean(satisfaction$satisfaction), 1),
              round(mean(satisfaction$loyalty), 1),
              names(sort(abs(cor(num_vars)[,"satisfaction"]), decreasing = TRUE)[2]),
              "4", max(table(clustering_results$kmeans$cluster)),
              paste0(round(lda_results$accuracy * 100, 1), "%"))
  )
  
  print(summary_data)
  
  return(summary_data)
}

exec_summary <- create_summary_table()

# Advanced correlation heatmap
create_correlation_heatmap <- function() {
  # Select key variables for cleaner visualization
  key_vars <- c("satisfaction", "loyalty", "recommendation", "expectations", 
                "quality", "service", "price", "trustworthiness")
  cor_subset <- cor(num_vars[key_vars])
  
  # Create heatmap
  par(mar = c(8, 8, 3, 2))
  image(1:ncol(cor_subset), 1:nrow(cor_subset), 
        as.matrix(cor_subset), col = heat.colors(20),
        main = "Korelace mezi jednotlivými ukazateli",
        axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
  
  # Add labels
  axis(1, at = 1:ncol(cor_subset), labels = colnames(cor_subset), 
       las = 2, cex.axis = 0.8)
  axis(2, at = 1:nrow(cor_subset), labels = rownames(cor_subset), 
       las = 2, cex.axis = 0.8)
  
  # Add correlation values
  for(i in 1:nrow(cor_subset)) {
    for(j in 1:ncol(cor_subset)) {
      text(j, i, round(cor_subset[i,j], 2), cex = 0.7)
    }
  }
  
  par(mar = c(5, 4, 4, 2))  # Reset margins
}

create_correlation_heatmap()

# Model performance comparison
model_comparison <- data.frame(
  Method = c("PCA", "Factor Analysis", "K-means", "LDA"),
  Key_Result = c(paste(pca_results$variance_info$optimal_components, "components for 90% variance"),
                 paste(ncol(fa_results$loadings), "factors explain 64.2% variance"),
                 paste("4 segments, silhouette =", round(clustering_results$silhouette_avg, 2)),
                 paste("94.4% classification accuracy"))
)

# Velikost vzorku
sample_size <- nrow(satisfaction)

# Rozložení podle pohlaví (pokud je ve sloupci "gender")
```

## Shrnutí

Analýza zkoumá vzorce spokojenosti mezi `r sample_size` zákazníky (`r female_count` žen, `r male_count` mužů) napříč službami a produkty. Využívá analýzu hlavních komponent (PCA), faktorovou analýzu a segmentaci zákazníků. Pro formulaci doporučení slouží i SWOT rámec. Analýza je zaměřena na zvýšení zisku zejména prostřednictvím vysoké spokojenosti zakázníků.

```{r echo=FALSE}
exec_summary <- create_summary_table()
```

Průměrná spokojenost dosahuje `r avg_satisfaction` bodů (rozmezí `r satisfaction_range`), průměrná věrnost činí `r avg_loyalty`. Silná korelace ukazuje, že růst spokojenosti přímo posiluje retenci zákazníků.  

```{r echo=FALSE}
create_correlation_heatmap()
```

---

## Klíčové poznatky

### Hlavní dimenze
- První komponenta PCA vysvětluje `r round(pca_results$variance_info$var_explained[1]*100,1)` % variability, což dokládá, že zákazníci hodnotí zkušenost celostně.  
- Šest faktorů vysvětluje `r round(sum(fa_results$loadings^2)/length(num_vars)*100,1)` % variance a pokrývá:  
  - spokojenost a zkušenost  
  - kvalitu služeb a produktů  
  - důvěru a reputaci  
  - loajalitu a doporučení  
  - šíři nabídky  
  - produktovou zkušenost  

### Segmentace zákazníků

| Segment              | Podíl % | Spokojenost | Věrnost | Riziko |
|----------------------|---------|-------------|---------|--------|
| Satisfied Champions  | vysoký podíl | vysoká | vysoká | nízké |
| Moderate Middle      | největší podíl | střední | střední | střední |
| Struggling Customers | menší podíl | nízká | nízká | vysoké |
| At-Risk Group        | nejmenší podíl | velmi nízká | velmi nízká | kritické |

Silhouette skóre = `r round(clustering_results$silhouette_avg,2)`, což potvrzuje smysluplné oddělení skupin. LDA model vykazuje přesnost `r round(lda_results$accuracy*100,1)` %.  

### Hnací síly spokojenosti
Nejvýznamnějšími faktory spokojenosti jsou:  
- očekávání zákazníků,  
- vnímané přínosy,  
- cena a vnímaná hodnota.  

---

## Strategické důsledky
- Zlepšení v jedné oblasti má multiplikační účinek díky vzájemné provázanosti hodnocení.  
- Největší příležitost představuje segment **Moderate Middle**, kde je prostor pro růst celkových výsledků.  
- Segmenty **Struggling** a **At-Risk** vyžadují okamžitý zásah ke snížení rizika odchodu.  
- Dlouhodobé zlepšení vyžaduje rovnováhu mezi kvalitou, hodnotou, důvěrou a cenou.  

```{r echo=FALSE}
create_presentation_plots()
```

---

## Spolehlivost modelu
- PCA redukuje data na `r pca_results$variance_info$optimal_components` komponent při zachování 90 % informací.  
- Faktorová analýza identifikuje stabilní dimenze vnímání.  
- Segmentace i LDA potvrzují robustnost a jasně vymezené skupiny zákazníků.  

---

*Analýza poskytuje jasný rámec pro řízení zákaznické zkušenosti a ukazuje, kde se vyplatí investovat do zlepšení.*
